messages:
maria: Heads-up — SylphTech's Dedicated commit keeps hitting us with long tail 'macrobursts' across regions after we pushed EU capacity last week. They expected traffic to stay local but spikes are shifting between us-east, eu-west, and ap-southeast over 6-12hr windows.
aj: Saw the same. Their 7d p95 shows two distinct modes: sustained daily baseline + intermittent multi-hour elevated periods. Those periods cause cross-region fallbacks and doubling of egress/model-sync.
aj: Quick snapshot from the projection I ran:
```
region    baseline_gpu_h   macroburst_gpu_h   pct_headroom_needed
us-east   1,200            1,800              +50%
eu-west   900              1,350              +50%
ap-south  400              1,000              +150%
```
maria: APAC swinging that hard explains why our safety band got eaten in <48h. Current policy is flat 20% buffer on committed pools — not working for skewed temporal patterns.
kai: Two operational problems: 1) cross-region model shard pulls multiply GPU-hours and egress costs; 2) autoscaler latency when drain/reassign happens during macroburst. We saw 4–6 min cold windows yesterday.
samantha: From customer side SylphTech says they won't increase committed base but will accept a short-term burst pool if we can limit cost exposure. They also asked for "regional tilt" allowance so they don't get penalized when traffic briefly moves to APAC.
maria: Proposed changes: dynamic regional safety bands + macroburst windowing. Idea: keep global reserved = committed, but allow per-region transient headroom pool that is: min(10% committed, 100 GPU) baseline + additional day/night multiplier based on historical tilt. That pool is metered separately and capped per-customer.
aj: Also propose a technical mitigation: warm-model-replica prefetch in likely target region when tilt probability > 30% for next 12h. That reduces cold-start and egress by keeping shards local for expected windows.
kai: Implementation notes: prefetching increases baseline memory/GPU residency; need a knob for eviction TTL and a fail-safe to avoid double-counting committed GPUs. Will require scheduler changes and a new metric: prefetched_gpu_seconds.
infra-bot: deploy-check: staging replay job queued (id: replay-246810). 48h replay will use traffic sampled from last 30d tilt events.
maria: Negotiation language for sales/legal: add "regional tilt allowance" clause: up to X GPU-hours/month from cross-region spikes will be billed at burst rate Y (discounted) and not counted against contract churn for SLA. Also define "macroburst protection window" (<=12h) where automatic short burst pool is allowed without churn.
samantha: I'll loop in AE + legal. SylphTech is open to a capped monthly burst SKU if we can guarantee <3x on-peak egress multiplier.
aj: Action items: 1) infra: run replay and surface prefetched_gpu_seconds + egress delta (maria/kai) 2) product: draft pricing language for regional tilt allowance (samantha) 3) infra & runtime: prototype prefetch TTL and eviction (kai/aj) 4) schedule 30m sync with SylphTech early next week (maria).
maria: I'll create the meeting and drop the replay results once infra-bot finishes. :calendar:
kai: One more ask — can we put a temporary cap on APAC burst to protect other customers in that AZ while we tune? suggest soft cap 400 GPUs.
aj: Agreed. Put it in staging as a circuit-breaker.
maria: cool — will update thread with replay output. thanks all. :thumbsup:
